newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota fieldwork slow to advance.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota fieldwork slow to advance.

text.p: Abundant moisture and a lack of warm weather continued to delay North Dakota fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop report.

Wet field conditions and colder than normal temperatures set the average starting date for fieldwork at May 9, five days later than the estimate in last week's report and well behind the five-year average of April 22.
There were some scattered reports of plantings, but as of Sunday state averages for spring wheat, oats and barley were less than one percent complete.
The five-year average of plantings shows 12 percent for spring wheat, 11 percent for oats and 10 percent for barley. Sugarbeets were three percent planted as of Sunday, versus 14 percent on average.
Workers continued to remove livestock carcasses from waterways across the state. The report said 770 carcasses had been removed from water and 5,688 carcasses had been buried.

Cattle conditions were rated three percent very poor, 13 poor, 31 fair, 51 good and two excellent. That compared to last week's rating of three percent very poor, 14 poor, 35 fair, 46 good and two excellent.
